thread:
sre-oncall: heads-up: apiserver 5xx spike in eu-central1 since ~06:15 UTC, leader election jitter and GPU attach queue climbing. NAT pool usage looks suspicious.
amy: can you paste a sample log?
sre-oncall: 
```
Jun 06 06:17:02 apiserver: 503 POST /api/v1/namespaces/default/pods  - "context deadline exceeded"
Jun 06 06:17:15 controller-manager: leader changed: prev=node-a, new=node-b
Jun 06 06:18:10 attach-controller: ERROR failed to attach GPU: timeout waiting for attach
```
jordan: checking cloud NAT metrics — ephemeral port exhaustion on eu-central1-nat-1, pool usage 98% (spikes aligned with attach bursts). infra-bot: @channel NAT pool usage 98% for eu-central1-nat-1. :warning:
kevin: attach-controller is retrying fast; we're hammering the control plane while cloud NAT drops connections -> attach timeouts. that cascades back to the autoscaler.
lucas: product impact?
product-ops: inference tail latency up ~2.4s for some customers, visible in canary and a couple of paid tenants. getting alerts.
amy: short-term mitigation suggestions: 1) throttle non-prod QPS to controlplane 2) reduce attach parallelism on autoscaler 3) request NAT pool expansion / port reuse config from cloud. who can action 2 & 3?
jordan: I will open an emergency ticket with cloud support for NAT pool expansion and ask for ephemeral port reuse settings. filing now.
kevin: i can push a quick config to autoscaler: lower concurrency and add exponential backoff. rolling change:
```
# autoscaler config snippet
gpu:
  attach:
    parallelism: 4
    backoffInitial: 5s
    backoffFactor: 2.0
```
sre-oncall: rolling that config as a canary to eu-central1. infra-bot: deploy started by kevin for autoscaler-config/eu-central1.
infra-bot: deploy succeeded (autoscaler-config/eu-central1) :white_check_mark:
amy: also temporarily banning non-prod namespaces from creating GPUs (policy toggle) to reduce noise. I'll coordinate with platform to patch policy.
lucas: mid-term proposal: reserve a small dedicated GPU pool in eu-central1 for critical workloads (warm nodes) to avoid attach on-demand spike. cost estimate: reserving 10 x p4-month ~ ~$28k/mo (ballpark), but would shave a lot of attach churn.
product-ops: that's a tradeoff we can present to customers vs risk. we need numbers vs observed outage minutes.
kevin: metrics while we rolled back autoscaler: attach failures dropped from ~120/hr -> ~18/hr in 20m, apiserver 5xx rate back to baseline.
sre-oncall: good. jordan: any update from cloud ticket?
jordan: cloud support acked, requested logs. they can increase NAT pool for us but need a config window; ETA 2h if we approve. also suggested reducing TIME_WAIT by enabling TCP reuse on gateways — requires infra approval.
amy: approve the change, let's do NAT pool expansion now — runbook step 3 approved. jordan please coordinate.
jordan: filing change request now, tagging @networking-team.
kevin: postmortem checklist: preserve CPU/attach-controller logs, collect NAT metrics, record autoscaler config change, and list the cost tradeoffs for reserved pool vs on-demand. I'll start the doc.
lucas: schedule a follow-up sync in 3h to decide whether to keep reserved pool.
product-ops: I'll draft customer-facing blurb if this impacts SLAs.
sre-oncall: monitoring for 30m. If 5xx stays low, we'll keep the throttles and autoscaler change for 6 hours then reassess. :thumbsup:
